approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only scores accepted in the current search session. It keeps a greedy population of up to 64 molecules, draws breeding parents from high-scoring quantile bands, and generates a fresh pool through connected-fragment crossover or ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations. Crossover can receive one finishing mutation. The Parent checks stable canonical identity and rejects duplicate proposals, then admits sulfur environments only when their signature multiplicity does not exceed the maximum in the original scored generating parents; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process over chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts learns from the complete accepted archive. Correlated posterior function draws select ten different pool members sequentially for real evaluation, and accepted feedback updates both the model and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add BRICS-typed single-cut crossover: choose one chemically defined cleavage from each actual scored parent, retain complete source components with the existing size preference, and join their retained endpoints only when the inherited release permits that environment pair. The intended change is better preservation of useful chemical context in distinct recombinants, measured through real gain magnitudes and later accepted descendants. Earlier children changed batch repulsion, pool width, reciprocal donor matching, parent-copy exclusion or ring construction. This variant changes cleavage and join support while retaining the outer breeding, finishing and selection laws. The parallel presence control separately measures complete crossover removal.

observed_bottleneck: Limited productive exploration is the observed bottleneck on actual code Parent n-1744a1494180. All three Parent summary.json/run.log pairs are present and successful: mean final Top-1 0.596453114288690, seed population SD 0.033970329983999, seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. The full downstream recount indexed in n-9b90d71cc6e1 reports 648 strict original-best-parent beats among 4350 actual Parent offspring, mean offspring score 0.372049560842182 against mean best generating-parent score 0.455304044833596, and 255 sequential incumbent increments totaling 5.819415048695712 across the panel. The Parent constructor cuts arbitrary non-ring SINGLE bridges and joins fragments without chemical endpoint typing; its molecular assessment still exposes reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and incomplete stereochemistry after the narrow sulfur gate. This does not prove unrestricted crossover causes the score limitation. Current-Parent DPP diversification n-9b90d71cc6e1 lowers mean by 0.038159276809506 despite separation and productive-core increases, and width40 n-fe16bf000919 loses 0.062417426521529 with 650 rather than 648 parent wins and lower dispersion. Count removal n-b9f2c3328d4c loses 0.038794771343121, supporting retention of occurrence information. Under the older ungated Parent, reciprocal compatible-donor sampling n-eb61315a5619, compatible/noncopy sampling n-bddb1dbe8e32 and two-cut ring construction n-870ed6964d46 lose 0.020270634588431, 0.102652730965678 and 0.045046288124129 respectively despite real useful recombinants. L07 reciprocal-context gating n-7ba291681388 nearly removes evaluated changed crossover and has only two complete seeds. These are contrary boundary evidence: type support, novelty, local wins and narrower dispersion cannot substitute for absolute progress and complete endpoint gain. The Parent deco_hop seed0 breakthrough at evaluation281 remains in the primary fifteen-cell comparison.

literature_review.conclusion: Read the frozen Search Policy literature review at .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r31-search-policy/literature-review.json, then searched and reopened the relevant primary BRICS and official RDKit sources using the actual queries above. The PubMed attempt supplied no usable original-paper text; publisher main-text access redirected to the abstract, while the primary-paper upload and publisher supplement were readable. Adopt the inherited-release chemical typing principle as this single fixed construction variant, preserving two scored sources and bounded rejection. Reject full fragmentation libraries, database screening, current-release substitution, donor conditioning, copy exclusion and a probability/rule sweep. No useful source establishes endpoint efficacy for this exact recipe. Slot1 uv verification loaded RDKit 2023.09.6, matched official source and inherited lock, checked 45 SINGLE rules and API boundary examples, and passively enumerated cuts on all 4500 archived accepted Parent rows: 228 rows lack an eligible cut. This static support is not actual pair compatibility, a scored offspring outcome or a counterfactual future. The review supplies a causal proposal and implementation provenance, not a performance or synthesis guarantee.

finding_summary.headline: Typed crossover supplies real descendants, but gains shrink and the mean drops by 0.0948
finding_summary.insights:
Release-defined cuts and intact raw source subgraphs create exposed, useful recombinants, but they did not increase productive gain under this optimizer. First new-core strict winners increased from 262 to 353, and the crossover subset increased from 59 to 82; all 82 typed-route winners were used as later breeders, with 68 producing accepted direct children. Yet their direct descendants supplied only 0.429 of sequential incumbent gain versus 0.975 for the Parent crossover cohort, and their transitive descendant unions supplied 2.924 versus 3.473. This narrows the failure beyond a lack of type exposure or complete suppression of reuse: more local successes and new cores do not establish more valuable search progress.

Local compatibility also leaves whole-molecule limitations unresolved. Finishing changed 429 of the 968 evaluated typed-route identities; only 693 retained an existential match to the entire immediate graph, and seven immediate joining bonds received different labels when re-perceived after sanitation. These are separate boundaries from the correctly typed raw construction. The molecular assessment still finds reactive attachments, unspecified stereochemistry and difficult ring geometry. One restarted docking session grew bulky sulfonamide-rich graphs and reached only 0.02898 while its matched Parent reached 1.00000; other restarted sessions produced compact amine/aryl leaders near 0.98. That is a coverage contrast, not proof that size, a specific attachment or the constructor caused that cell loss.

The matched result rejects the proposed gain benefit for this fixed recipe and satisfies its registered stopping condition. It supports a negative total contribution of this construction variant under these conditions; it does not decide whether crossover presence is beneficial, identify separate contributions of cleavage, compatibility, RNG history or finishing, or establish chemical mediation. The Parent late decoration breakthrough remains in the primary comparison, and excluding that one cell descriptively still leaves a mean loss of 0.08462.
finding_summary.results:
The typed construction executed correctly on all 43,402 crossover attempts. It made 26,677 valid immediate products, including 20,302 that differed from both parents; 968 typed-route final molecules were evaluated, 797 from distinct immediate recombinants and 171 from parent copies changed by finishing. All mapped raw contexts and permitted single joins checked correctly, and every pool and batch completed.

The number of accepted offspring beating their original best parent rose from 648 to 675 out of 4,350, but their gains became smaller: positive parent margins totaled 13.55 versus 17.25, and sequential incumbent improvements totaled 4.40 versus 5.82. Mean accepted score fell from 0.37205 to 0.34186 while the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.45530 to 0.40198. The complete matched final Top-1 mean fell from 0.59645 to 0.50166, a change of -0.09479 against the required +0.002. All three seed means declined; 12 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined and seed dispersion increased from 0.03397 to 0.08873.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic products retain reactive attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; one seed grows bulky sulfonamide-rich graphs
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-55d120396e72 produces indole/azaaryl amide and amidine families, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, aryl-substituted cyclic amines, interconnected amine/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated nitrogen-rich dione/imino systems. Rings and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9931-1.0 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.9793-1.0. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are zero in every digest task. Neutral notation does not imply absent protonatable amines. There are different chemical families between objectives and seeds, with repeated local variants among leaders; moderate diversity is a qualitative reading rather than an efficacy metric. Recognizable amides, ethers, carbonyls and cyclic amines coexist with direct N-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O connections whose plausibility depends on their full environment, electrophilic peripheral groups, and difficult small-ring or bridged unsaturation. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable and drug-likeness weak overall, although some compact outputs are more recognizable medicinal chemistry.

All 15 Child and all 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectory paths were present and read: each node has 4,500 accepted records, including 4,350 optimizer observations and the repeated initial observations. Every objective has all issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 accepted observations per session. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, no profile mismatch, and baseline_type=code_parent. No task, path or matched-seed comparison is missing. The digest's final excerpt is late seed-2 proposals, not the complete set of seed endpoints; the full trajectories supply the other endpoints below. Published Parent trajectories are the comparison authority, not convenience aliases or additional realizations of an ancestor. All complete SMILES in cited_smiles are actual Child digest or trusted Child trajectory entries. Parent chemistry is described by published task/seed/evaluation references without adding Parent-only SMILES to that citation list.

Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 perception of the accepted optimizer rows finds direct N-halogen bonds in 1,018 Child observations versus 786 Parent observations, and potentially stereogenic unassigned centres in 2,769 versus 2,455. No assigned centre is perceived in either output set. These are structural counts derived from the shown trajectories, not new scores. In contrast, the Child has no optimizer molecule with at most three heavy atoms, versus 82 in the Parent: historical tiny-fragment coverage is substantially narrowed, while excess elaboration remains visible. Path hashes, molecule descriptors and exact observed counterpart pairs are documented under .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r31-slot1-molecular/.

This assessment concerns accepted final graphs. It does not reconstruct rejected attempts, unevaluated pools, immediate typed joins, finishing changes or breeding ancestry. The bound intent explicitly allows ordinary mutations and finishing after a typed construction; the chemistry of an accepted output cannot identify its constructor route or certify that the final molecule retains a typed join. No conformers, synthesis routes, protonation study or independent stereochemical labels were supplied. Score gradients below are associations among observed molecules, not target definitions, affinity measurements, component attribution or mechanism-activation decisions. The recurring local-group, geometry, stereochemistry, context and alternative-family gaps retain the provenance recorded in the published n-1744a1494180 molecular report: earlier n-c55c3d520a2c findings carried through n-62daf219c70a, then re-observed here under this current matched Search panel. Historical conditions and results are not pooled or re-estimated by the present molecular assessment.

per_task.generated_character: All optimizer observations contain ring-closure and aromatic text; halogen-string incidence is 0.9402. The seed-0 leader has 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings: a fused five/seven-membered system connected through N-N to an N-formyl pyridyl substituent, plus alkenyl chloride, vinylic bromine and alcohol. Seed 1 leads with a 24-heavy-atom indole/ether-ring anilide containing direct amide N-F; N-Cl and N-Br counterparts also appear. Seed 2 leads with a 26-heavy-atom dimethoxy/vinyl indole aryl amidine carrying N-F and aryl F. These are compact aromatic/polar arrangements, but the unusual N substitution weakens their apparent synthetic plausibility. Published Parent leaders instead have 24-25 heavy atoms and three rings, with azaindole/indole N-hydroxy amides or an adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl linkage. An N-hydroxy amide and an N-halogen amide are distinct chemical environments.
liabilities: Direct N-F/N-Cl/N-Br occurs in 439 of 870 accepted optimizer observations, versus 275 in the Parent, including high-scoring anilides and amidines.
The best seed-0 N-N/formamide connection, halogenated alkenes and other altered fused-ring variants need assessment of complete functional-group context and geometric accessibility.
missing_features: Consistent conventional substitution retaining the favorable compact aromatic/polar arrangement is not established at the leading labels. The actual N-H counterpart is available but lower-scoring; an exact missing target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
Defined stereochemistry is absent where new saturated ring/carbinol centres arise. The seed-0 best has a perceived unassigned centre; no stereochemical label comparison was supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed-0 evaluation 279 reaches 0.4588069837338257, seed-1 evaluation 149 reaches 0.45555627303128626, and seed-2 evaluation 122 reaches 0.41605207864642335. The exact seed-1 N-F/N-Cl/N-Br anilide series at evaluations 149/163/193 shares 0.45555627303128626; its actual N-H counterpart at evaluation 180 scores 0.40465559506276. Thus this local label gradient tolerates reactive N substitution and does not establish conventional chemistry as the score maximizer. Small methoxy fluoroarenes score 3.135095803976772e-11, while a 44-heavy-atom doubled indole/anilide at seed-2 evaluation 32 scores 1.2598632247894483e-14. Complete compact aromatic/polar organization matters more than either fragmentation or added aromatic mass in these examples. Parent maxima for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Late Child molecules explore N-halogen amines, thioamides and altered rings below the seed leaders; their presence does not demonstrate a useful new family.

per_task.generated_character: Ring and aromatic text incidences are both 0.9977. Seed 0 develops linked azaaromatic carbonyl/thione and ether systems: its 32-heavy-atom leader has five perceived rings, including a three-membered closure against aromatic atoms, fluorinated alkoxy groups and aryl chlorine. Seed 1 reaches a much larger 46-heavy-atom, four-ring nitrogen-rich framework with exocyclic ethylidene groups, N-formyl/amidic substituents, an aldehyde and aryl bromine. Seed 2 favors a 33-heavy-atom, seven-ring N/O-rich dione framework with halomethyl ether, N-N/N-O connections and several perceived three/four-membered closures. The different families demonstrate available chemical breadth, while strained topology and reactive peripheries make their synthesis questionable. Published Parent chemistry includes a compact 30-heavy-atom linked azaaryl carbonyl/thione seed-0 leader, a nitrile/cyanate/S-Br family in seed 1, and a nitroso/small-ring family in seed 2; Parent leaders are not synthesis certificates either.
liabilities: The seed-0 best has a perceived three-membered ring containing an aromatic edge; seed-2 leaders have multiple perceived small rings. This flags geometry questions without making all fused or small rings unacceptable.
Seed-1 best combines extensive N-formyl/amidic elaboration, aldehyde and halogen mass; seed-2 output includes halomethyl ethers and N-N/N-O contexts. These require environment-specific assessment.
missing_features: Reliable access to an equally favorable complete heterocyclic arrangement with conventional peripheral groups and credible ring geometry is not shown. The much higher Parent seed-0 label identifies a coverage limit, not an exact absent target motif or a component cause.
Stereochemical and conformational identity remains unresolved for the connected-ring and substituted-chain leaders; more ring closures or more nitrogen does not supply it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed-0 evaluation 298 reaches 0.6190015479876161; seed-1 evaluation 296 reaches 0.6181404528260512; seed-2 evaluation 241 reaches 0.6053048745966144. In contrast, a nine-heavy-atom fluorinated acyclic amino-diene scores 0.5017480989424001, a ten-heavy-atom acyclic polycarbonyl nitrogen fragment scores 0.503082071151814, and a reduced 17-heavy-atom fused heterocycle in seed 0 scores 0.5281738239562879. Linked complete heterocyclic arrangements are associated with the higher labels; atom count or heteroatom count alone cannot explain them. Published Parent seed-0 evaluation 281 reaches 0.8561477222467935 with a different linked azaaryl/thione arrangement; that late Parent gain remains in the comparison. per_task.generated_character: All accepted optimizer graphs contain rings; aromatic-string incidence is 0.9966 and halogen incidence 0.9977. Seed 0 reaches a 29-heavy-atom aryl/azetidine/bridged tertiary-amine leader with aryl Br, two aryl F atoms and an aniline. It has five perceived rings, including two four-membered cycles and constrained unsaturation. Seed 2 reaches a 35-heavy-atom diaryl cyclic-amine/sulfinamide arrangement bearing an imine, methoxy, amino and N-bromoamino groups. Its four perceived rings and six perceived unassigned centres leave geometry and stereochemical identity unresolved. Seed 1 is chemically different: median optimizer size is 78 heavy atoms, with a 69-heavy-atom, seven-ring best containing six chlorine atoms, two N-sulfonyl ring nitrogens, an ester, formamide and a long unsaturated thiol-bearing chain. That best has calculated molecular weight 1123.86 and is far outside compact ordinary medicinal chemistry. The published Parent seed-1 best is instead a 28-heavy-atom diaryl seven-membered diaza ring with available amines and methylthio substitution.
liabilities: The seed-1 output expands bulky chlorinated N-sulfonyl structures while labels remain low; excessive size and many nitrogen atoms do not substitute for useful functional relationships.
High-label seed-0 rings include constrained four-membered unsaturation, while seed-2 leaders retain N-Br, imine and sulfinamide contexts. Stable geometry and synthesis were not demonstrated.
Potentially stereogenic unassigned centres occur in 867 of 870 Child optimizer observations; assigned configurations were not supplied.
missing_features: Consistent access across restarted seeds to compact aryl-connected, available cyclic-amine arrangements is missing. Such molecules are already produced in two Child sessions and in the published Parent; adding nitrogen indiscriminately is not the supported gap.

Defined stereochemistry and credible conformations of the successful bridged/ring systems are absent. Neutral SMILES does not establish their physiological protonation or a missing charge-centre capability.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best, a 39-heavy-atom N-sulfonyl/carboxylic-acid/amide framework, scores 0.01904115112334333. Child seed-0 evaluation 269 reaches 0.9871003578204819 and seed-2 evaluation 290 reaches 0.9773324390416854, where compact aliphatic amines and aromatic regions coexist. A smaller N-sulfonyl cyclic ester at seed-0 evaluation 19 scores 0.00016747245492913543, and an amine-free biaryl alcohol at evaluation 20 scores 0.0017422851854604245. This supports the presentation of available cyclic amines with aryl regions, not nitrogen count alone. Child seed-1 evaluation 287 reaches only 0.028978154856197657 despite extensive growth and multiple nitrogen atoms; sulfonylated nitrogens are chemically different from ordinary basic amines. The published Parent maxima for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. The seed-1 difference is a structural coverage contrast between adaptive sessions, not identified mediation by size, amine availability or a constructor component. The strong Child seed-0 leader has no direct N-halogen bond, demonstrating that this liability is not required for a high label.

per_task.generated_character: All optimizer graphs have ring-closure text; aromatic incidence is 0.9966 and halogen incidence only 0.1115. The seed-1 best has 30 heavy atoms and five perceived rings: ethoxyaryl and phenyl regions joined through a ten-membered nitrogen/carbonyl ring with N-methyl groups and tertiary-amine/imide functionality. Its oxygen-containing four-membered closure against an aromatic region is unusual. Seed 0 instead reaches a 33-heavy-atom connected aryl/ether/amine/dicarbonyl system with four perceived rings, including eight- and nine-membered cycles. Seed 2 favors a 31-heavy-atom, five-ring cross-connected aryl amine/lactam framework with an N-O linkage and exocyclic unsaturation. These are nitrogen/carbonyl-rich structures, not a shortage of amides or rings. The published Parent includes quinoline-linked nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring systems and another connected azaaromatic family; all have unverified synthetic and geometric access.
liabilities: The best seed-1 family carries an aromatic-adjacent four-membered oxygen closure as well as a medium nitrogen ring; seed-0 and seed-2 families have cross-connected medium rings and constrained unsaturation.
N-O and N-N variants appear late. Their plausibility depends on complete local and ring context, rather than a blanket objection to every N-O or N-N bond.
missing_features: Geometrically credible, simpler alternatives preserving the favorable aryl/amine/carbonyl relationships are not established consistently among leaders. Several functional-group-rich connected-ring families already exist; no exact missing target motif is supported.
Specified stereochemistry and conformational identity remain absent where aryl-bearing saturated and ring-junction centres arise; carbonyl/ring abundance does not resolve those identities.

per_task.generated_character: Ring-closure incidence is 0.9931, aromatic incidence 0.9793 and halogen incidence 0.8885. liabilities: Direct N-halogen occurs in 467 of 870 accepted optimizer observations versus 425 in the Parent, including the seed-1 and seed-2 leaders.

Aldehyde, halomethyl, imino and thiol/ketone groups occur in high-label families, with environment-dependent reactivity. Small connected carbocycles and unassigned centres add distinct geometry and identity questions.
missing_features: Conventional, stereochemically defined peripheral alternatives retaining the favorable compact polar/fluorinated arrangement are not consistently established at the leading labels. A successful N-halogen-free seed-0 family exists, so a universal need for reactive N substitution is unsupported.

No uniform absent donor or basic-amine requirement follows from these outputs: the overall best has no perceived hydrogen-bond donor, while other strong families have imino and hydroxyl donors. An exact target scaffold cannot be inferred from the supplied scores.

Child seed-0 evaluation 273 reaches 0.5355440503801135, seed-1 evaluation 257 reaches 0.5487604283327778, and seed-2 evaluation 232 reaches 0.5954294421753954. transferable_gaps.evidence: This repeats the local-group concern sourced in the published n-1744a1494180 report from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a. The current source is n-55d120396e72 versus n-1744a1494180 under the issued Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per objective and inherited original-parent sulfur admission conditions. Direct N-halogen appears in 1,018 of 4,350 Child optimizer rows versus 786 Parent rows. The observed anilide CCc1c2cc3[nH]c(C(=O)N(F)c4ccccc4)cc3c1OCC2 scores 0.45555627303128626, while its actual N-H counterpart scores 0.40465559506276. Conversely, a compact aryl cyclic-amine leader without N-halogen reaches 0.9871003578204819 and another N-halogen-free polar family reaches 0.5355440503801135. A typed construction is therefore not a certificate of the final graph's functional-group integrity; these observations do not identify the generating component or re-establish the historical sulfur-envelope counts.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently offer conventional complete functional-group environments around successful molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent complete local functional-group context and offer conventional alternatives preserving useful relations learned from current accepted observations, including when subsequent edits change that context. Distinguish aryl halogens from N/O/S-halogen attachments and assess N-N, N-O, imino and sulfur groups by their full environment. Preserve successful ordinary chemistry. The output does not justify a universal motif ban, an external answer library, or a claim that a broader filter improves endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Geometry concerns retain their n-c55c3d520a2c to n-62daf219c70a to n-1744a1494180 provenance and are re-observed in n-55d120396e72 on this complete matched Search panel at 300 observations per objective. The 0.6190015479876161 linked heterocyclic leader has a perceived three-membered closure against aromatic atoms. The 0.22946728879623843 aryl/amine/dicarbonyl leader has an oxygen-containing four-membered aromatic-adjacent closure and a ten-membered nitrogen ring. A 0.9871003578204819 cyclic-amine leader has constrained four-membered unsaturation. Other leaders use medium rings without that same local pattern, so the gap is conditional on topology and unsaturation, not missing rings or universal implausibility of a ring size. No conformers or synthesis routes establish feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can build many rings but does not consistently distinguish valence-valid closures from geometrically credible connected-ring structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep useful ring-containing arrangements while making closure, bond-order and reconnection choices sensitive to ring size, bridge connectivity and accessible geometry. Offer feasible alternative connectivities without prohibiting all small, fused, medium or macrocyclic rings. Aromatic labels and permitted local joins do not settle whole-molecule geometry; no component attribution or endpoint benefit follows from this structural association alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereochemical gap reported for n-c55c3d520a2c and carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 persists in n-55d120396e72 under this current matched profile, Search seeds 0/1/2 and 300 observations per objective. Every supplied digest stereocentre-string incidence is zero. Read-only RDKit finds unassigned centres in 2,769 of 4,350 Child optimizer observations versus 2,455 Parent observations, with no assigned centre perceived in either set. The compact 0.9871003578204819 bridged cyclic-amine leader has three perceived unassigned centres, and the 0.5954294421753954 fluorinated dione leader has two. Some aromatic leaders have no such centre, so this does not apply indiscriminately to every emitted molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic generated arrangements remain unspecified even in compact high-label molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or specify chemically meaningful stereochemistry through graph edits and distinguish stable configurations from achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Investigate protonation and tautomerism separately: neutral notation coexists with ordinary protonatable amines. The supplied observations establish an identity gap, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a constructor-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This narrows the fragmentation/excess-elaboration gap traced by n-1744a1494180 to n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a. Current n-55d120396e72 output, compared with the published n-1744a1494180 Parent on the issued 300-observation Search sessions, contains no optimizer molecule with at most three heavy atoms, versus 82 in the Parent. The tiny-fragment subtype is therefore not reproduced here. Excess elaboration is: one restarted session has median size 78 heavy atoms and a 69-heavy-atom chlorinated/sulfonamide-rich best at 0.028978154856197657. Its same-objective counterparts in other Child seeds have compact 29/35-heavy-atom cyclic-amine leaders at 0.9871003578204819 and 0.9773324390416854; the paired Parent seed has a 28-heavy-atom diaryl diaza-ring leader at 0.9999994532254913. In other observed families, simple aryl fragments and large doubled heterocyclic structures both lose useful relationships. These differing adaptive histories do not isolate size or nitrogen availability as a mediator.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group context is preserved unevenly when molecular growth or simplification changes the surrounding structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use current-session feedback to retain productive relationships between aromatic regions, available amine centres and polar groups while allowing chemically useful growth and simplification. Distinguish nonacylated amines from sulfonylated or amidic nitrogens. Neither a fixed size cutoff nor adding nitrogen or aromatic mass is a supported solution, and the existing compact successful outputs must remain visible as counterexamples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This continues the conditional alternative-family concern documented in n-1744a1494180, sourced from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a, with fresh evidence from n-55d120396e72 under the complete current matched Search panel. High-label series repeatedly vary halogens, short chains or local ring segments; the observed N-F/N-Cl/N-Br anilide trio has exactly the same 0.45555627303128626 label. Distinct families do appear between seeds, including strong N-halogen-free and compact amine structures, so the output is not globally scaffold-collapsed. Yet one session remains in a bulky low-label family and another linked-heterocycle session never reproduces the much higher published Parent arrangement. String novelty and many rings therefore do not establish reliable useful chemical coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically credible independent alternatives to successful local families are not represented consistently across restarted searches.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically distinct, feasible connectivities preserving favorable functional relationships learned from the current session, and assess their chemistry and observed labels separately. This is a conditional capability gap; it does not prescribe an objective answer, an external molecule library, a particular selection or constructor change, or a guaranteed benefit from increasing diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
